name: Foundation leaks
title:
A leak is a clue.
Look at the whole picture.
summary: Understand where water is entering, the conditions around the wall, and the protection your space needs.
body: A recurring wet corner changes how you use a basement. Start with the pattern: where water appears, when it arrives, and how the surrounding property handles it. Bring the visible leak into a wider conversation about the foundation, access, drainage, and existing repairs.
details: The water path
Describe the affected wall or floor edge, rain patterns, and any changes you have noticed.
The surrounding site
Bring photos of accessible grading, downspouts, window wells, and nearby paving.
The proposed scope
Ask which water paths the work is intended to address and what remains outside the proposal.
Life after the work
Discuss restoration, future finishing plans, access, maintenance, and written terms.

name: French & trench drains
title:
A better path
for the water.
summary: Bring surface runoff, subsurface collection, and the final discharge into one clear drainage plan.
body: Where water collects matters. So does where it goes next. French drains and grated channel drains address different collection needs. The starting point is a site-specific conversation about runoff, below-grade conditions, access, and a suitable outlet—not simply choosing a drain by name.
details: Collection
Show where water pools or crosses a surface, and whether the concern is above or below grade.
Conveyance
Ask how the collection points connect and how existing buried drainage will be evaluated.
Discharge
Clarify the destination and who confirms the applicable local requirements.
Maintenance
Understand what must remain accessible, how the system is checked, and who restores the site.

name: Concrete foundations
title:
Build confidence
below grade.
summary: Coordinate concrete foundation protection while the plans, surfaces, and construction sequence can still be shaped.
body: The best-looking room begins with decisions made long before its finishes. For a below-grade concrete project, discuss the wall and slab assemblies, water-management approach, transitions, and construction timing together. Keep important details visible until they have been addressed.
details: Current plans
Bring the latest drawings, site information, and any specified waterproofing details.
Transitions
Identify wall-to-slab connections, penetrations, joints, changes of level, and adjacent assemblies.
Trade coordination
Agree who owns each detail and what must be checked before it is covered.
Documentation
Ask for the final scope, product information, installation records, and pre-cover photographs.

name: Crack injections
title:
Small opening.
Important questions.
summary: Separate a water-sealing objective from a structural concern before discussing a targeted repair.
body: A visible crack is a starting point, not a diagnosis. Its location, material, history, moisture pattern, and any movement all belong in the assessment. Ask what a proposed injection is designed to achieve and whether additional evaluation is needed.
details: Context
Photograph the entire wall as well as the opening. Include older photos or repair records when available.
History
Record when you first noticed it, any visible change, and the conditions when water appears.
Repair objective
Clarify whether the proposal addresses leakage, structural performance, or an assessed combination.
Limitations
Ask what the repair does not cover and when a structural professional should be involved.

name: Underslab & wraps
title:
Before the pour.
Beyond the surface.
summary: Bring underslab moisture protection and waterproofing wraps into the project before access becomes limited.
body: The layers beneath a slab do different jobs. Clarify vapor control, capillary breaks, and any required waterproofing performance with the project team. Then coordinate the selected assembly, its penetrations, protection during construction, and inspection before it disappears.
details: Performance
Ask which moisture conditions the specified assembly is intended to address.
Continuity
Coordinate edges, columns, pits, and service penetrations—not only the open field of the slab.
Sequence
Discuss readiness, protection from damage, and checks before concrete or backfill conceals the work.
Handover
Retain the drawings, material information, approved changes, and photographs of completed details.

name: Showers, spas & pools
title:
Beauty above.
Consideration beneath.
summary: Plan the waterproofing conversation for showers, spas, mikvahs, and pools around the actual use of the space.
body: A refined finish is only one part of a wet-area project. Bring the intended exposure, heat or steam conditions, substrate, drain connections, and construction stage into the conversation. Each type of space needs its own suitability assessment; a shower detail is not automatically a pool detail.
details: Intended use
Describe the room, expected water exposure, and any specialty operating conditions.
Complete assembly
Discuss floors, walls, corners, entrances, penetrations, and the drain as connected details.
Coordination
Confirm the responsibilities of the design team and installation trades before finishes are ordered.
Verification
Discuss the specified system’s inspection or testing procedure and the records provided before concealment.
